description: Synthetic research corpus for pipeline validation, not a claim about real papers or general retrieval quality.

chunks.text: AlphaNet uses a convolutional backbone and a feature pyramid network to detect small objects. Multi-scale feature fusion combines shallow high-resolution details with deeper semantic features.

chunks.label: Figure 3
chunks.text: Figure 3. AlphaNet architecture: convolutional backbone, feature pyramid, and three prediction heads for small, medium and large objects.

chunks.label: Table 2
chunks.text: Table 2. Small-object detection AP: AlphaNet 31.2; baseline 25.0. Both use the same training data and evaluation split.

chunks.label: Table 4
chunks.text: Table 4. Ablation study: full AlphaNet small-object AP 31.2; without feature pyramid AP 27.1; without multi-scale augmentation AP 29.0. Each ablation removes one component.
AlphaNet limitations: evaluation is restricted to daylight street scenes. Night-time performance and deployment latency were not measured.
BetaDet uses a vision transformer backbone with patch tokens and a single prediction head. It does not use a convolutional feature pyramid.

chunks.label: Table 1
chunks.text: BetaDet small-object AP is 33.0 on the common daylight street benchmark. AlphaNet AP is 31.2 under the same data split and evaluation protocol. BetaDet requires more memory.
BetaDet inference latency is 42 ms per image on the reported GPU. CPU latency was not measured. This result cannot establish CPU deployment speed.
Hybrid retrieval combines normalized dense embeddings and BM25 lexical ranking using reciprocal rank fusion. RRF adds one divided by a constant plus the rank from each result list.
The agriculture survey studies irrigation schedules and seasonal rainfall. It contains no object detection experiments.

questions.question: Which components make up the AlphaNet architecture in Figure 3?
questions.reference_answer: AlphaNet uses a convolutional backbone, a feature pyramid, and three prediction heads.

questions.question: Compare AlphaNet small-object AP in Tables 2 and 4.
questions.reference_answer: Full AlphaNet scores 31.2 in both tables. Removing the feature pyramid reduces AP to 27.1; removing augmentation reduces it to 29.0.

questions.question: Which performs better on small object detection, AlphaNet or BetaDet?
questions.reference_answer: BetaDet scores 33.0 versus AlphaNet 31.2 under the same evaluation protocol.

questions.question: Why does the ablation support using a feature pyramid?
questions.reference_answer: Removing the feature pyramid lowers small-object AP from 31.2 to 27.1 in the controlled ablation.

questions.question: What night-time evaluation limitations are reported for AlphaNet?
questions.reference_answer: AlphaNet was tested on daylight street scenes; night-time performance was not measured.

questions.question: How do reciprocal rank fusion and BM25 contribute to hybrid retrieval?
questions.reference_answer: BM25 supplies lexical ranking. RRF combines its ranks with dense retrieval ranks using inverse rank contributions.

questions.question: Can BetaDet's GPU latency establish CPU deployment speed?
questions.reference_answer: No. The reported 42 ms result is on a GPU and CPU latency was not measured.

questions.question: Compare the backbones and prediction heads of AlphaNet and BetaDet.
questions.reference_answer: AlphaNet uses a convolutional backbone, feature pyramid and three heads. BetaDet uses a vision transformer and one head.
